thread:
elaine: Heads-up — we ran into a blocked prod deploy during the EU change window yesterday. deploy-bot rejected the job citing missing MFA for the user. Can we confirm the current policy on who is allowed to prod-deploy during change windows?

samir: I saw the same. Deploy was queued by @maria for the hotfix and deploy-bot returned `403: MFA_REQUIRED`. Not sure if it's an account config or role membership.

deploy-bot: NOTICE: Deploy request 2025-10-02T22:11Z by user=maria rejected. Reason=MFA not satisfied. Required: mfa:true AND role in [prod-deployer, infra-oncall]. Refer to docs/internal/deploy-perms.md

maria: I had MFA on but maybe it's the hardware key check. I used a TOTP app earlier. Did we switch to security key only for prod?

elaine: TL;DR — policy changed two weeks ago to require hardware-backed MFA (security keys) for accounts with prod-deployer role. This was supposed to be staged but looks like it hit production. I didn't communicate the rollout well enough, apologies.

tony: Oof. We should not surprise folks during a change window. Immediate ask: can someone with admin perms temporarily grant @maria the prod-deployer role with an MFA-exempt flag for this single deploy? Or we run the hotfix from an approved admin account.

samir: We have two possible safe paths: 1) Escalate to an on-call infra admin to run the deploy for the hotfix (no role change needed), or 2) Issue a short-lived role grant with documented justification and audit ID. Prefer 1 for minimal blast radius.

maria: I can wait 15–20m if an admin can run it. If not, I'll request temporary elevation. What's the approved process for short-lived grants?

elaine: Approved process: open a ticket in #eng-oncall, label it "prod-deploy-elevate", include PR link, reason, and approver. Then an infra admin uses authctl to grant a role with TTL and records the audit ID. Example command we use: ```
# grant 1 hour prod-deployer for maria
authctl grant --user maria --role prod-deployer --ttl 1h --reason "hotfix EU cache bug"
```
Make sure the ticket includes the approver's Slack message (prod release manager).

deploy-bot: ACTION: To avoid future surprises, scheduled enforcement change was rolled out. Affected users must have `mfa:hardware` attribute true in SSO profile to be considered. See /docs/security/mfa-rollout.

tony: Can we add a temporary exception window for change windows where secondary verification (manager approval) can suffice if security key not present? We rely on engineers in regions that don't have keys issued yet.

elaine: Long-term, yes — but not without compensating controls. Short-term fix: I can authorize a one-off exception for the EU change window tomorrow if we produce a list of users who need exceptions and they get manager approval in-thread. Exception will be logged and auto-revoked.

maria: If you can add me to the exception list I have the PR link ready: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/4321 — Hotfix: shard map fallback. Approver: @samir.

samir: I approve this elevation for @maria for the single deploy. Logging: ticket #ENG-8427. maria, once uplifted, please run the deploy and confirm in this thread.

elaine: Done — added maria to temporary-exception group with TTL 1h. deploy-bot should accept the next request.

deploy-bot: NOTICE: Temporary exception applied. User=maria flagged mfa:exception until 1749003723. Deploy requests by maria will bypass hardware MFA check. Audit=ENG-8427.

maria: Starting deploy now. 

maria: deploy-bot: `start deploy prod service-shard-map 2025-10-02T22:30Z`

deploy-bot: ACTION: Deploy job 7891 accepted. Running preflight checks...

deploy-bot: INFO: Preflight OK. Rolling out to EU region canary (10%)

deploy-bot: SUCCESS: Canary healthy. Promoting to 100% in 2m

deploy-bot: SUCCESS: Deploy complete. Version pinned: service-shard-map@v2.14.3. Latency regression: +0.2% (within tolerance).

maria: Confirmed. Post-deploy checks passing. Thanks for the quick turn. :party_parrot: 

elaine: Thanks all — follow-ups: 1) We need clearer comms when security-enforced changes roll out (I'll draft an announcement for infra and eng-releases). 2) Inventory of folks without security keys and a rollout schedule. 3) Update the prod-deploy runbook with exception flow and the exact commands.

tony: Also suggest adding an automated pre-deploy check that warns users in Slack if their SSO attributes won't pass the deploy-bot before they click deploy. Prevents wasted attempts.

samir: Agreed. I'll open a ticket to add that check to the deploy CLI and web console, plus a UX hint in the PR template.

elaine: Filed ENG-8432 for pre-deploy SSO validation and ENG-8433 for comms + runbook update. Closing this thread once docs are updated.

maria: Thanks, everyone. Learned about the hardware MFA requirement the hard way. 

elaine: And great job keeping it low-risk. We'll make the process less painful. :thumbsup:
